result:
that file.

One test relies on a naming assumption. The pipeline must call `internal.check_profile` through the module attribute. I patch both `internal.check_profile` and `pipeline.check_profile`, so a direct import by name also works.

Test functions:
- `test_explain_uses_a_five_worker_thread_pool_and_matches_the_sequential_run`: `explain` builds a `ThreadPoolExecutor` with `max_workers=5`. Mode, headline, segments, disclaimer and section order equal a sequential run even when the lanes finish in reverse order (§20.10, D8.2).
- `test_explain_output_is_independent_of_lane_timing`: opposite lane delays give byte-identical explanations (D8.2).
- `test_non_pass_sections_really_overlap`: the three non-pass lanes sit inside narration together on three distinct worker threads, never the caller's. A barrier proves it with no timing (§20.10).
- `test_total_wall_time_is_well_under_the_sum_of_section_sleeps`: three lanes sleeping 0.4 s each finish in under 0.8 s, against a sum of 1.2 s (§20.10).
- `test_exception_in_one_lane_falls_back_to_the_template_and_keeps_the_others`: when `narrate_section` raises for `risque`, that section gets the template, the others keep their results, order holds, `explain` doesn't raise, and the mode is `template` (§20.10, §20.5).
- `test_real_narration_with_one_failing_writer_keeps_the_other_sections`: with the real `narrate_section` and a writer exception on `risque`, `horizon` and `contraintes` stay `llm`. `risque` falls back to the template and passes V1–V5, and pass sections never reach the writer (§20.5, §20.10).
- `test_pass_sections_make_no_llm_call_in_the_lanes`: only non-pass sections call the writer, once each. A cache miss on `contraintes` leaves the others unaffected (§20.5).
- `test_robert_report_has_the_profile_coherence_block`: the report block is exactly `{status, findings}`. On Robert it is status `warning` with C1 (rule) then N6.1 (llm), with fr and en questions and no `violation`, equal to `check_profile(profile, "2026-11-12")` (§20.9).
- `test_review_calls_check_profile_once_with_the_portfolio_as_of`: one call per review, with `as_of` equal to `portfolio.as_of`, not the clock (D1, §20.9).
- `test_profile_coherence_never_changes_verdict_or_section_status`: with `check_profile` returning 3 warnings, the verdict, section statuses, checks, unknowns and explanation headline and mode are unchanged. It runs on both Robert portfolios, `coherent` and `incoherent` (§20.9, D3).
- `test_report_with_the_new_block_is_schema_valid_and_the_block_is_required`: `profile_coherence` is in `required` and `properties`. A report without it is rejected. `pass`, `info` and `warning` validate, while `violation` and a missing status are rejected (§13, §20.9, invariant 3).
- `test_report_with_three_warnings_validates_against_the_schema`: the finding shape (`values` for rules, `quotes` for N6) validates (§13, §20.9).
- `test_audit_records_the_n6_call_and_its_gate_status`: the audit has exactly one `profile_consistency` entry in `llm_calls`. It has the call-log keys, gate `accepted`, and fields matching the call log `check_profile` returns (§10, §20.9).
- `test_audit_carries_the_gate_status_whatever_it_is`: a `rejected:evidence` gate status is logged as-is, with the input hash (§10, §11).
- `test_reports_are_deterministic_apart_from_the_run_id`: two reviews give identical report text once `run_id` is masked, and the block is present (invariant 8).
- `test_cli_review_prints_one_profile_line`: `cli review` prints exactly one unindented line, `profile: warning (C1, N6.1)` (§12).
- `test_cli_review_profile_line_lists_the_finding_ids_in_order`: the line format is `profile: <status> (<ids joined by ", ">)`, shown with `C2, C3, N6.1` (§12).
- `test_cli_demo_prints_a_profile_line_per_review`: `cli demo` prints the profile line once for each of Robert's two reviews. The Amira and Mateo fixtures are incomplete, so they produce none (§12, D7).

I marked the ambiguous choices with `# SPEC-AMBIGUITY:` comments where they occur.
